title: The sabbath was made for man (Mark 2:13–28)
hookLine: he eats with sinners and says rest serves people, not the reverse

lines: A DAY OFF, FULL OF GUILT.
cards: A day off, and the laptop is open on the couch. Chores get done so the day counts for something. "I'm resting," said like an apology.
Rest can start to feel like a reward nobody has quite earned. In today's reading, Jesus gets into two arguments: one about who he eats dinner with, one about a day of rest and what it's for.
And he settles it with one sentence.

teach.h: LEVI AND A TABLE OF SINNERS.
teach.b: First, the dinner. Jesus walks past a tax collector named Levi, sitting at his booth, and says follow me, and Levi does. Mark sets tax collectors right beside sinners, which tells you how people saw them.

Jesus eats at Levi's house with a crowd of tax collectors and sinners, and people object. He answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "They that are well have no need of a physician, but they that are sick." Second, the word.
Sabbath is the Hebrew shabbat, from a root meaning to stop, to cease.
In Genesis, God rests on the seventh day, and the commandments tell Israel to keep it holy and to let everyone rest: children, servants, foreigners, even the animals. Third, the argument.

On a sabbath, Jesus's disciples pluck heads of grain as they walk through a field. Some Pharisees object that this is work. What counts as work was a real question in Jewish teaching, asked seriously.
Jesus answers with a story about David, who ate the holy bread when his men were hungry. Then the sentence: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath."

teach.h: REST IS A GIFT, NOT A BURDEN.
teach.b: Rest is a gift for people, not a burden laid on them.

teach.h: THE SABBATH WAS MADE FOR MAN.
teach.b: Jewish teachers said something very close; a later rabbinic teaching puts it: the sabbath is given to you, not you to the sabbath. Fourth, what Catholics do with it.
Christians came to gather on Sunday, the day of the resurrection, and Catholics keep it as the Lord's Day: Mass, and rest from needless work.

how: Catholics keep Sunday as the Lord's Day by attending Mass and resting from unnecessary work, and the Church teaches that Sunday rest is meant for family, prayer and care for others.

games.q: your friends are hungry and pick grain as you walk through a field on the sabbath. some teachers object that it's work. what does Jesus say?
o: the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
games.why: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." he doesn't dismiss the day. he says what it's for.

practice: For these two minutes, you're not improving yourself or getting anything done; you're stopping, which is what sabbath means. If a to-do list shows up in your head, let it go past, and let your shoulders and your jaw drop.
If you pray, receive this rest as a gift from God; if you don't, just receive it.

wordCard.voice: Sabbath. From the Hebrew shabbat, to stop: the day of rest, which Jesus says was made for people. Today's word.
